note: Labels for the builder set. Written before any run, like the other one. This set is not used to score clustering — truth.json does that — so the labels here exist to say which needs a correct builder should be able to close, and with what.

needs.description: Look up a Pokemon's type and base stats by name
requests: look up a pokemon by name and get its stats
pokemon base stats and type from its name

needs.description: Facts about a country: capital, population, currency, region
requests: facts about a country by name
population and capital of a country
what currency and capital does a country use
country information including region and languages

needs.description: Photographs of a named dog breed
requests: show me photos of a specific dog breed
get images for a dog breed by name

singletons: what will the weather be tomorrow in lisbon
how tall is the ground at these coordinates
generate a qr code for a url
what_this_measures: Whether the builder closes a need that CAN be closed. The other set cannot answer that, because every need in it is unclosable and the builder fails all of them for the same reason.
Whether the duplicate check correctly refuses the four singletons, which existing tools already answer.
what_this_does_not_measure: Clustering quality. truth.json measures that, on a set written for it.
Whether real people would phrase things this way. One author, as before.
